extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for handling amendments and replies after a final rejection and after allowance (including timing, entry/no-entry standards, form paragraphs, hand delivery, expedited processing under 37 CFR 1.116, and amendments under 37 CFR 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview after final
rubrics_metrics.description: One personal interview by applicant may be entertained after a final action; only one request by applicant after final should be granted, but in exceptional circumstances a second personal interview may be initiated by the examiner if in his or her judgment this would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews after final are exceptional; examiner may initiate a second interview only if it would materially assist in placing the case in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include claim variants at filing/first reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include, at the time of filing or no later than the first reply, claims varying from the broadest to the most detailed that the applicant is willing to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing claim variations early can alleviate prosecution difficulties and is beneficial for both Office and applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required final-rejection shortened statutory period (form wording)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each final rejection must include the specified wording informing applicant that a shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire three months from the date of the action and setting out the treatment when a first reply is filed within two months and advisory action timing; and that in no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than six months from the date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual includes exact form-paragraph text (form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.40.01, 7.41, 7.41.03, 7.42.09) that examiners must use to advise applicants of the shortened statutory period and how extension fees will be calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of first reply within two months on SSP and extension fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months from mailing of a final rejection and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the 3-month shortened statutory period, then for purposes of determining any extension fee the period for reply will be the date the Office mails the advisory action, but in no event later than six months from the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advisory action mailed before 3 months, shortened period expires at 3 months; if mailed after 3 months, it expires on advisory mailing date. If first reply not filed within 2 months, extension fee is calculated from end of reply period set in final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to reply during shortened period causes abandonment unless extended
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a reply during the shortened statutory period results in abandonment of the application unless the time is extended under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must timely file or obtain an extension under 1.136 to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry is not a matter of right after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116) or reinstate previously canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only certain limited amendments (e.g., canceling claims, adopting examiner suggestions, removing issues for appeal) that require only cursory review may be entered without the showing required under 1.116(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing required for amendments after final (37 CFR 1.116(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where an amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or otherwise requires only cursory review, compliance with the requirement of a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(c) is expected in all amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide the proper showing will support refusal to enter the amendment; refusal should not be arbitrary and should be concisely stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible replies under 37 CFR 1.113 after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to: (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116; (B) a Notice of Appeal (and appeal fee); or (C) a request for continued examination (RCE) filed under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission that meets the reply requirement of 37 CFR 1.111 and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant patent applications filed before June 8, 1995 and design applications; follow statutory/regs for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution application (CPA) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Further examination may be obtained by filing a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d), if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA practice does not apply to utility or plant applications if the prior application has a filing date on or after May 29, 2000; see MPEP § 706.07(h) and § 201.06(d) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entry related to appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection but before an appeal brief may be entered upon or after filing of an appeal brief provided the total effect of the amendment is to (A) remove issues for appeal, and/or (B) adopt examiner suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an amendment is entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must indicate which individual rejection(s) in the action from which the appeal was taken would be used to reject the new or amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No recognition of conditional authorization to charge appeal fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO does not recognize 'conditional' authorizations to charge an appeal fee if an amendment submitted after a final Office action is not entered; any such conditional authorization will be treated as an unconditional payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not attempt to provide conditional authorizations; they will be processed as unconditional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of a 'clean' set of claims (37 CFR 1.121(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 by presenting a clean set of all pending claims in one paper; 1.121(c)(3) provides for optional submission of a clean (no markings) version of pending claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidating previous versions into a single clean set is beneficial; parenthetical identifying previous versions should not be repeated. If the paper contains no changes, it should be entered; if it includes amended claims with a marked-up version, the examiner may choose not to enter the amendment due to 1.116 considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty when amendment doesn't place case in better form
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal nor in condition for allowance, applicant should be promptly informed of this fact, whenever possible, within the statutory period. The refusal to enter should not be arbitrary and reasons should be concisely expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily the specific deficiencies need not be discussed, but concise reasons such as those in examples (A)-(D) should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common concise reasons for non-entry (examples A-D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical concise reasons for non-entry include: (A) proposed claims would not avoid rejections in last Office action; (B) proposed claims would raise new matter; (C) proposed claims present new issues requiring further consideration or search; (D) proposed amendment presents additional claims without canceling finally rejected claims, so it does not place the case in better condition for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reasons should be used to explain non-entry; they need not be exhaustive but should identify the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim status indication by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment, and which proposed claims would be entered on the filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entered for appeal purposes, the examiner must indicate on the advisory action which individual rejection(s) from the action being appealed would be used to reject the new/amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice to applicant about partial acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should be notified if certain portions of the amendment would be acceptable as placing some claims in better form for appeal or complying with objections or requirements if filed in a separate paper; similarly, notify if some amended claims would be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps assure filing of a brief consistent with claims as amended and may avoid unnecessary appeals; a statement that the final rejection stands and the statutory period runs from the date of final rejection is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Advisory Action form PTOL-303
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply from applicant after final rejection where the reply is prior to filing of an appeal brief and does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-303 advises applicant of disposition of proposed amendments and the effect of any argument or affidavit not placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness goals for examiner action on after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from receipt by the examiner; a reply to such an amendment should be mailed within 30 days of receipt by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is placed in condition for allowance, issue Notice of Allowability PTOL-37 promptly; if processing delays occur and statutory periods are near, notify applicant by interview and mail an Interview Summary PTOL-413. Make every effort to mail before reply period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment if no appeal or entry making allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be alerted promptly to avoid inadvertent abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.181 petition does not stay reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply to an examiner's action which may be running against an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on a 1.181 petition to extend reply deadlines; follow appeal and post-appeal procedures in MPEP § 1207.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and use of form paragraphs 7.67-7.80
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.67-7.80 are to be used when issuing advisory actions after a final rejection; choose the appropriate paragraph(s) based on specific facts (e.g., first reply filed within 2 months, variable SSP, appeal filed, amendment to be entered, amendment not entered, reasons for non-entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examiner notes in each form paragraph for bracket insertions, sequencing (e.g., 7.67 must precede 7.70), and special instructions (do not use for reexamination proceedings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for specific advisory paragraphs refusing entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs address grounds for refusing entry, including: lack of showing why amendment necessary and not earlier presented (7.72); raises new issues requiring further consideration/search (7.73); amendment not improving form for appeal (7.75); additional claims without canceling corresponding finally rejected claims (7.76); proposed new claims would be allowable only if filed separately (7.78); affidavits/exhibits considered but do not overcome rejection (7.79); affidavits/exhibits not considered for failure to show earlier presentation (7.80).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using these paragraphs, follow the examiner notes to identify claims, provide explanations, and include transitional provisions if applicable (e.g., 37 CFR 1.129(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper may be personally delivered to a Technology Center (TC) only if (1) the paper is accompanied by some form of receipt which can be handed back to the person delivering the paper; and (2) the examining group being asked to receive the paper is responsible for acting on the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receipt may be a card containing identifying data (applicant name, application number, filing date, description). TC will date-stamp and return receipt; if paper contains a check or authorization, TC will hand-carry to Office of Finance and then process and enter the paper into the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of hand-delivered papers with fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If a hand-delivered paper is accompanied by a check or contains an authorization to charge a Deposit Account or credit card, the paper will be accepted and date-stamped, but hand-carried by TC personnel to the Office of Finance for processing, then made an official paper in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cash/checks/money orders are hand-carried to Customer Service window; processed by accounting clerk for pickup at 3:00 p.m. next work day; upon return to TC papers entered into application file wrappers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing for replies under 37 CFR 1.116 (Box AF)
rubrics_metrics.description: An expedited processing procedure exists for amendments/replies under 37 CFR 1.116. To use it, the amendment must be marked 'Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Technology Center (Insert Technology Center Number)' on the upper right of the paper and the envelope must be marked 'Box AF' in the lower left corner. If mailed, the envelope should contain only 1.116 replies and be addressed to 'Box AF, Assistant Commissioner for Patents, Washington, D.C. 20231.' Replies may alternatively be hand-carried to the TC and similarly marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings should be prominent (bright color). Mail Center will specially process 'Box AF' envelopes and forward promptly to TC. Upon receipt, designated technical support will forward to examiner via the SPE. The USPTO goal is to mail the examiner's action within 1 month from receipt of the amendment/reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities and troubleshooting for expedited procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPE is responsible for ensuring prompt action on expedited replies; if assigned examiner unavailable, SPE ensures prompt action. If no action is received within the stated timeframe plus normal mailing time, applicant should telephone the SPE; if unsatisfactory, contact the TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to use the procedure correctly; it will not overcome delays caused by the applicant (e.g., delayed interviews, further replies, petitions requiring decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle practice (amendments after allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims have been allowed, prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex parte Quayle). Amendments touching the merits after allowance are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection; prosecution may be continued as to formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 to issue a Quayle action listing formal matters to be corrected and setting a shortened statutory period for reply (two months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendment received after mailing of Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that reaches the Office after the notice of allowance has been mailed has the status of one filed under 37 CFR 1.312; its entry is a matter of grace. If received by the Office prior to mailing but not received by the examiner until after mailing, it has the same standing as though the notice had not been mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application has not been closed to further prosecution, applicant may be entitled to have such amendment entered even if withdrawal from issue would be necessary; withdrawal is unnecessary if the amendment is of a type the examiner would recommend entry for under 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 amendments after allowance (requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the notice of allowance. Any amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee and may be entered on recommendation of the primary examiner, approved by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of amendments that fall within 1.312 include amendments to the specification, changes in drawings, amendments to the claims, changes in inventorship, submission of prior art, etc. The amendment must be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid. Approval authority for recommendations under 1.312 is delegated to SPEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of supplemental oaths/declarations after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of a supplemental oath or declaration submitted in a reissue, a supplemental oath or declaration is not treated as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312. A supplemental reissue oath/declaration is treated as an amendment under 1.312 because it effects correction of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applicants submitting a supplemental reissue oath/declaration after allowance must comply with 1.312 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner authority after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance has been mailed the application is technically no longer under the primary examiner's jurisdiction, but the examiner can make examiner's amendments and has authority to enter amendments submitted after Notice of Allowance that are merely corrections of formal matters in the specification/drawings, formal matters in a claim without changing scope, or cancellation of claims, without forwarding to the SPE for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive amendments after allowance generally require SPE/Commissioner approval under 1.312; formal corrections can be handled directly by primary examiner per MPEP § 1302.04.
